data.title: Apple's 9-9 event 'most consequential iPhone launch' in decade as Ternus takes over: MS
data.description:
Apple's (AAPL) September 9 fall product launch event, "Surprise and Shine," might stand as its most significant in nearly a decade, according to the analysts at Morgan Stanley.

"Apple's 'Surprise and Shine' product launch event next Wednesday should follow a very similar format to past years—a 90-minute presentation of Apple's newest device introductions, namely the Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, AirPods 5, iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max, and, most importantly, its first foldable iPhone," said Morgan Stanley analysts, led by Erik Woodring, in an investor report.

"However, the event will prove to be anything but ordinary. This is because for the first time in 15 years, Tim Cook will not headline the event; instead, new CEO John Ternus will lead the company into its first major iPhone form factor change in nearly 10 years, unveiling the much-anticipated iPhone Fold (Ultra?), alongside what are likely to be the broadest and most significant, like-for-like iPhone price hikes in company history," he added.

If Apple's first foldable phone captures a positive reaction from consumers, it could contribute significantly to revenue for the December quarter.

"We currently forecast ~6.5M foldable iPhone shipments in the December quarter, translating to ~$14B of revenue, or 16% of total December quarter iPhone revenue," Woodring noted. "Beyond the near-term financial contribution, it will be worth watching how Apple leverages the larger form factor and whether it delivers use cases that are better on a foldable vs. simply a larger screen—and most importantly, how the device really feels in hand. If consumer reception is strong, we believe the category could ultimately become larger than current supply chain forecasts imply."

Another critical point to consider is how consumers will react to price hikes across the new iPhone lineup. Morgan Stanley expects like-for-like iPhone Pro price increases will range from $200 to $500. The financial firm expects the 512GB foldable iPhone will start at $2,399 and the 2TB model will go for $3,199.

"With NAND and DRAM costs rising sharply, we continue to expect Apple to raise the starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max by $200, with potentially larger increases at higher storage tiers," Woodring said. "Based on our memory cost forecasts for Apple, such pricing actions would allow Apple to maintain iPhone gross margins of ~40%, broadly in line with the FY21-FY25 average of 39.9%."

data.title: Anthropic IPO launch pushed toward mid-October: Reuters
data.description:
One of the world's most anticipated initial public offerings is facing a slight delay. Artificial intelligence company Anthropic (ANTHRO) is expected to start marketing its much-sought-after IPO in mid-October at the earliest, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The maker of the Claude chatbot is expected to complete the listing days before the U.S. midterm elections in November, according to the people who added that ⁠the plans, including the timing, could change.

Anthropic (ANTHRO), which was expected to make its IPO prospectus public as early as next week, marking the final stages of the listing, is now not expected to complete that step until late September, two of the people said.

The changes are not unusual, as companies frequently revise their IPO timelines depending on the market environment, regulatory feedback, and other conditions. Anthropic (ANTHRO) declined to respond to Reuters’ request for comments.

As part of the listing, the company is also planning to finalize a $15B revolving credit facility before meeting with analysts, including those at banks ‌financing the transaction, one of the people said.

The Financial Times reported on Friday that Morgan Stanley (MS) and Goldman Sachs (GS) are in talks with Anthropic (ANTHRO) to secure top roles in the offering, which is widely expected to value the company at more than $2T.

data.title: NFL preview: Sportsbooks take on the prediction market challenge; SCOTUS wildcard?
data.description:
The NFL season begins next week when the defending champion Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots on September 9. An equally intriguing match-up this season will be the sports betting sector versus the prediction market industry.

Sports betting is legal in some form in 39 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico, while 32 states have legalized online wagering. However, major markets such as California and Texas still do not allow conventional online sportsbooks, which opened the door for prediction markets such as Kalshi (KALSHI) and Polymarket (POLYMARKET) to gain a significant foothold, despite efforts by DraftKings (DKNG) and FanDuel (FLUT) to cut into the impact by introducing prediction market platforms of their own in some geographic markets.

Despite the new challenge from prediction markets, analysts expect sports betting revenue to top last year's tally of $30B for the NFL season, with the addition of Missouri to the sports betting mix helping to provide a boost. Notably, DraftKings (DKNG) and FanDuel (FLUT) are more promotional with sign-up incentives, reactivation offers, and profit boost offers than they were going into the week of the NFL last season. 

For the 2026–27 season, the NFL has renewed and expanded its official commercial relationship with sportsbooks. The league announced multiyear agreements with DraftKings (DKNG), FanDuel (FLUT), and Fanatics Betting and Gaming (FANA). DraftKings (DKNG) and FanDuel (FLUT) have held official NFL betting relationships since 2021, while Fanatics (FANA) joins the group under the new arrangement. The partnerships provide brand and marketing rights, but they also signal that the league continues to treat licensed sportsbooks as its primary commercial betting category.

For investors, licensed sportsbooks are still seen as a solid bet since they retain NFL partnerships, well-developed mobile products, brand clout, and responsible-gaming obligations. Prediction markets offer another route to NFL exposure, including in some states without online sportsbooks, but face numerous court cases and state-level enforcement uncertainty that could result in a Supreme Court showdown in 2027. If the prediction market industry survives the court challenges, the expectation is that Kalshi (KALSHI) and Polymarket (POLYMARKET) could become serious IPO candidates.

data.title: U.S. approves potential $5.75B in weapons sales to Saudi Arabia
data.description:
The U.S. State Department said ​Friday it ‌approved the potential sale of ​Joint Direct Attack ​Munitions-Extend Range to Saudi ⁠Arabia for ​an estimated $5B and a separate potential sale of AGT-1500 engines to Saudi Arabia ​for an ​estimated $750M (I, II).

Saudi Arabia has requested to purchase 5,000 KMU-572 Joint Direct Attack Munition guidance kits; 5,000 KMU-556 JDAM guidance kits; 5,000 BLU-111 500-lb general purpose bombs; 5,000 BLU-117 2,000-lb general purpose bombs; 60 AGT-1500 tank engines; and related equipment, the U.S. government said.

"The proposed sale will improve Saudi Arabia’s airborne defense capability to counter current and future regional threats, strengthen its homeland defense, and improve interoperability with systems operated by U.S. forces and other Gulf Region partners," the State Department said.

Boeing (BA) and Honeywell (HON) will be the principal contractors for the JDAM-ERs and AGT-150 engines, respectively.

data.title: U.S. Gulf-to-China VLCC shipping rate reportedly hits record high
data.description:
The rate for a Very Large Crude Carrier shipment from the U.S. Gulf Coast to China hit a record high, Argus reported Friday, on strong Asia-Pacific demand driven by the escalation of hostilities between the U.S. and Iran in the Persian Gulf.

Commodity trader ST Shipping put the VLCC Helios on subjects for a U.S. Gulf-to-China loading from October 13-16 at a $29.75M lump sum, including $250K in load-port fees, equivalent to $14.29/bbl, which Argus said represents the highest level since it began its U.S. Gulf-to-China assessment in November 2017.

Japanese commodity trader Idemitsu reportedly put the Maran Apollo on subjects for a U.S. Gulf-to-Japan voyage at $29.25M, including load-port fees, and Equinor (EQNR) and Occidental Petroleum (OXY) both put VLCCs on subjects for elsewhere in the Asia-Pacific region at $27.65M each, including load-port fees, according to Argus.

Charterers reportedly have put at least 10 VLCCs on subjects for Asia-Pacific voyages from the U.S. Gulf Coast since August 31, including the latest four.

Crude oil futures rose modestly on Friday ahead of the Labor Day holiday weekend, closing out a week of strong gains that saw the resumption of U.S. strikes on Iranian targets and Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, sparking fears that Persian Gulf flows might be constrained into next year.

The U.S. average retail price of diesel hit $5.85/gal on Friday, the highest on record, according to AAA data; a year ago, prices averaged $3.712/gal.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia’s decision to keep the price of its flagship Arab Light crude grade to Asia—the largest market for Middle Eastern oil—unchanged for next month at a $2/bbl discount to the Oman/Dubai benchmark suggests "the market is not as tight as thought," ING analysts said in a note.

Prices for grades sold to Northwest Europe and the Mediterranean were also left unchanged, while U.S. customers saw a $1/bbl increase.

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for October delivery edged up 0.2% to $91.48/bbl, front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for November delivery added 0.8% to $96.28/bbl, and front-month Nymex October natural gas (NG1:COM) gained 2.1% to $2.975/MMBtu.

For the week, Nymex crude, Brent crude, and Nymex natural gas rose 9.7%, 9.3%, and 3%, respectively.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), gained 2.2% this week.

ETFs: (USO), (BNO), (UCO), (SCO), (USL), (DBO), (DRIP), (GUSH), (USOI), (UNG), (BOIL), (KOLD), (UNL), (FCG), (XLE)

data.title: Bloom Energy surges on inclusion to S&P 500; Illumina, Everpure also added
data.description:
Bloom Energy (BE) jumped 6.2% post-market Friday after the manufacturer of solid oxide fuel cell systems for on-site power generation was added to the S&P 500, along with Illumina (ILMN) and Everpure (P); Bloom Energy had surged 7.5% in the regular session in anticipation of the S&P 500 selection.

Illumina (ILMN) and Everpure (P), which were upgraded from the S&P MidCap 400, rose post-market by 1.7% and 2.1%, respectively.

The three additions to the S&P 500 replaced Molson Coors Beverage (TAP), The Trade Desk (TTD), and Builders FirstSource (BLDR), which were all dropped down to the S&P SmallCap 600.

Added to the MidCap 400: HubSpot (HUBS), AGNC Investment (AGNC), Corcept Therapeutics (CORT), and Brinker International (EAT).

Deleted from the MidCap 400: Boston Beer (SAM), Capri Holdings (CPRI), Illumina (ILMN), and Everpure (P).

Added to the SmallCap 600: Herc Holdings (HRI), Delek US Holdings (DK), AXT (AXTI), Arcutis Biotherapeutics (ARQT), Boston Beer (SAM), Capri Holdings (CPRI), Molson Coors Beverage (TAP), The Trade Desk (TTD), and Builders FirstSource (BLDR).

Deleted from the SmallCap 600: N-able (NABL), Shenandoah Telecommunications (SHEN), Matthews International (MATW), Verra Mobility (VRRM), Franklin BSP Realty Trust (FBRT), NexPoint Residential Trust (NXRT), Amerisafe (AMSF), Cogent Communications (CCOI), Corcept Therapeutics (CORT), and Brinker International (EAT).

data.title: Stardust Solar Energy launches $641,000 private placement
data.description:
• Stardust Solar Energy (SUNXF) on Friday announced a non-brokered private placement of up to 641 senior secured convertible debenture units for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $641,000.
  • Each debenture unit will consist of one senior secured convertible debenture of principal value $1,000 and 8.55M common share purchase warrants.
  • The company intends to use the net proceeds of the offering for its solar project in Zambia, as well as for general and administrative, marketing, and working capital purposes. 
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: L3Harris Technologies lands $139M contract boost to supply Navy submarine masts
data.description:
• L3Harris Technologies (LHX) won a $139M contract modification to produce low-profile photonics masts, spares, and engineering support for new and in-service submarines.
  • The work will be performed in Northampton, Massachusetts, and is expected to be completed by September 2030.
  • The contract is fully funded  at award, with Navy funds from shipbuilding, procurement, and national sea-based deterrent programs.
  • The obligated funds will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year, providing funding visibility through the contract period.
  • The Naval Sea Systems Command is the contracting activity.

data.title: General Dynamics wins big with $149.6M U.S. Navy ship contract
data.description:
• General Dynamics (GD) said its NASSCO unit won a $149.6M contract to maintain, modernize, and repair the USS Pinckney (DDG 91).
  • The contract covers labor, equipment, testing, and other work needed for the ship’s Fiscal 2026 Depot Modernization Period.
  • The contract includes options, which if excercised could bring contract’s total value could reach $149.9M.
  • The work will be performed in San Diego, California, and is expected to be completed by September 2028.
  • The $149.6M contract will be fully funded at award, mainly through $135.8M in Navy procurement funds, while $12.9M in operations and maintenance funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year.
  • The Naval Sea Systems Command is serving as the contracting activity.

data.title: Boeing gets $241.34M contract boost to repair Navy fighter aircraft
data.description:
• Boeing (BA) said on Friday that it received a $241.34M contract modification to repair flight control surfaces used on Navy F/A-18 E/F and EA-18G aircraft.
  • The modification covers 9 different configurations of flight control surfaces, with work expected to be completed by September 2032.
  • A total of $60.34M, or 25%, in fiscal 2026 Navy working capital funds will be obligated at the time and will not expire by the end of the current fiscal year.
  • An additional $181.01M remains committed to funding the delivery order, which has a maximum value of $241.34M.
  • Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon Systems Support is the contracting activity.
